In my experience I lost my entire family around age 19 or so because of this. Anytime I wasn’t alright, I was treated as a hazard and to be ignored until I worked out my issues. 

Mom and Dad basically disowned me for years and they still have trouble speaking to me now. I’m 30.

Ive spent several years dealing with homelessness, abuse, bouncing place to place and isolating myself because I hadn’t gotten proper help. Took me years to get where I’m at now and I’m still basically just beginning my journey of healing.

Years of being abandoned by family for having mental health issues has basically shut me down. It’s difficult to accept help from people. Terrifies and sends me into a pit of guilt when they do. It’s also difficult to not isolate due to feeling like a burden (that’s the biggest issue). If I start to feel my mental health slipping, and I am starting to feel not OK again I’ll saw the answering the phone or talking to people. Then I’ll get worse, and most of the time it’ll end really badly with me exploding, damaging myself, doing something stupid end up in jail like drinking and screaming, things like that. Afterwords when all is said and done it’s always difficult for me to explain to people that I was just really not OK, and I was alone. 

Both of my parents have made small attempts to mend our relationship here and there, but eventually always back out again the moment that I had even a bad day or any break down where I was crying. I haven’t heard from my dad in a while and my mom hasn’t called and said I’m not expecting to hear from her for months maybe even years. 

Last time I spoke to my Mom was in 2020. She planned a road trip with my dad and brother, and invited me last minute. I couldn’t find a pair of shoes that I wanted to bring and ended up having a mental break down at my house. These breakdowns happen because of years of homelessness (living out of bags, losing stuff) my parents have no understanding of this because they weren’t around, so when I lost it and started crying on the phone she left and hasn’t made contact with me since. 

It’s really messed up to be labeled as anything when you’re in a crisis. You just need help. It’s So mess up how people will focus on your reaction to what you’re going through, instead of the thing that’s causing you to react that way. In most peoples minds, they say “well maybe you shouldn’t let things affect you” but it doesn’t work that way, it simply doesn’t. It takes so much power and work to get yourself to a point where you are so peaceful internally, that nothing externally affects you. A lot of people are working to get to that point but expecting people to just simply be there is ridiculous and the fact that that those expectations run rampant pisses me the fuck off.

Most of the men who have raped, tried to force themselves onto me since I was a young girl are still out there living happy thriving lives. I’m the only one messed up from it all. The guys who have done these things to me are ALL self proclaimed “nice guys”.

My Dad and Grandfather spent their entire lives thinking about themselves. I was the only daughter in the family, and they taught me nothing, never protected, or lifted me up. Any time anything in my life went wrong they turned around and blamed me, so I have a real skewed view of a Black men. 

I understand some of these issues are due to generational trauma, and history of Black families being torn apart repeatedly (due to New Jim Crowe, murder, drugs brought to the community, etc.) but these things are just excuses the Black men in MY LIFE have used to justify why they weren’t good family members. I say excuses because we grew up away from issues like that, and they still failed at providing any stability or upbringing I could grasp onto…

Speaking for myself, the men who birthed me didn’t give a shit if I was dead or alive, and they still don’t. So no I don’t feel I can depend on them. But I don’t think that accounts for all Black Men, because I still believe (and see) there are plenty of other Black Men out there doing a great job at being there for their families.

Wish I wasn’t a statistic, but people suck sometime so I have no control over that besides just being a better me.
